study_identification_part.si_4_title: Fractionating autism based on neuroanatomical normative modeling

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study used the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP) dataset, a multi-center dataset collected across 6 sites: King's College London (UK), University of Cambridge (UK), Radboud University Nijmegen Medical Centre (Netherlands), University Medical Centre Utrecht (Netherlands), Central Institute of Mental Health Mannheim (Germany), and University Campus Bio-Medico Rome (Italy).
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "We included 206 neurotypical (NT) (79 female, aged 17.5 ± 6.1 years) and 316 participants with autism (88 female, aged 17.2 ± 5.7) including mild intellectual disability participants across 6 sites from the EU-AIMS LEAP sample"

answer.LEAP (Autism cohort, N=316): clinical application (normative probability map estimation, spectral clustering for subtyping, and clinical/genetic association analyses)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The NT cohort (N=206) was used to estimate the normative model of cortical thickness using Gaussian process regression with 10-fold cross-validation. The autism cohort (N=316) was used to generate normative probability maps (NPMs), which were then subjected to spectral clustering to identify neuroanatomical subtypes, followed by clinical, behavioral, and polygenic score association analyses.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206) using the following covariates...We used 10-fold cross-validation during the training process to provide an unbiased estimation of the model...We then created/calculated NPMs for participants with autism, which quantify the deviation of regional CT from the expected neurotypical pattern (N=316)."

model-1.model-name: Gaussian process regression normative model of cortical thickness
model-1.train-phase: NR (10-fold CV used; approximately 185 per fold)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was built using Gaussian process regression on the entire NT cohort of 206 participants with 10-fold cross-validation. The overall phase includes all 206 NT participants. The exact train-phase N per fold is not explicitly reported, but with 10-fold CV it would be approximately 185-186 per fold.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: "We included 206 neurotypical (NT) (79 female, aged 17.5 ± 6.1 years)...GPR was trained on the NT cohort (N=206)...We used 10-fold cross-validation during the training process to provide an unbiased estimation of the model."

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The overall NT cohort had a mean age of 17.5 years (SD=6.1). The age range of the entire LEAP sample (NT + autism) was 6-31 years as stated in the abstract. Since train-phase statistics per CV fold are not reported separately, they are marked NR. Min and max are inferred from the sample-wide age range of 6-31 years reported in the abstract.

dc_5_sex_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The NT cohort consisted of 206 participants, of whom 79 were female. Male N was inferred by subtraction: 206 - 79 = 127. Female percentage: 79/206 = 38.3%. Male percentage: 127/206 = 61.7%. Train-phase sex breakdown per CV fold is not reported.
